text: Castration can be done at any age up to 12 months, but is best done young, before 2 months. Burdizzo: crushes blood vessels to cut off blood supply to the testicles, killing them; clip one spermatic cord at a time, at different levels for each cord, to preserve blood circulation in the scrotum itself. Rubber rings: an elastic band cuts off blood supply so the scrotum and testicles eventually fall off; usable only in calves under 3 weeks old, and calves must be vaccinated against tetanus and blackleg beforehand. Surgical castration: wash hands, boil instruments, and disinfect the scrotum with iodine beforehand; use a sharp knife to remove the lower third of the scrotum (needed for proper drainage), pull the testicle through the incision, cut the white membrane, and separate the testicle from the tough spermatic cord (containing artery, veins, and cord) — in calves, the vessels can simply be pulled until the strand breaks.
